title: 'Maxxing' Named Dictionary.com's Word of the Year
paragraphs: Trying to get more sleep, eat more protein or look your best? There's now a word for taking each of those goals to the extreme: "maxxing." And the trend has become so popular that Dictionary.com has named it its Word of the Year for 2026.
Short for "maximizing," maxxing means doing something to the fullest, or trying to make one part of your life as good as possible. It can be used on its own, but is usually added to another word.

So, "looksmaxxing" is about improving your appearance, while "sleepmaxxing" means trying to get better rest. At work, "tokenmaxxing" means using as much AI as possible. Even spending a quiet evening at home can become "cozymaxxing."

While the term has been around in different forms for a long time, it's the rise of "looksmaxxing" that brought it into wider use and helped popularize the spelling with an extra "x." According to Steve Johnson, Dictionary.com's director of lexicography, its use in the media has risen by more than 1,000% since the start of 2026.

To choose its Word of the Year, Dictionary.com looks at how often a word appears in news articles, on social media and in online searches. But the team also looks for a word that captures something distinctive about the year.
Johnson believes "maxxing" captures the pressure many people feel, especially online, to keep doing more and becoming better at everything, from work and school to health and appearance.
"If there is an aspect of life that could be improved, it can probably be maxxed," health researcher Jennifer Donnelly wrote in The Conversation.
But Donnelly warns that the constant drive for self-improvement can also lead to unrealistic expectations and stress.
Other words Dictionary.com considered for this year's title included "affordability," "data center," and "unc" — a shortened form of "uncle" used to refer to an uncool older adult.
